section_summary.extract_value: The abstract describes a single (unnamed) study that examined how cognitive fusion and body appreciation relate to the association between body image discrepancy and disordered eating in a sample of 369 women, controlling for BMI. Results indicate greater body image discrepancy is associated with more disordered eating, and this relationship is partially mediated by higher cognitive fusion related to body image and lower body appreciation. The abstract does not report participant demographics (country, age, race), recruitment source, measurement instruments (BAS/BAS-2), BMI values, or correlations between body appreciation and BMI.
section_summary.evidence_source: Summary based on the provided abstract sentences: (1) aims and sample: "...the present study aims... in a sample of 369 women." (2) main results: "Results indicated that women who perceived their body as significantly discrepant... show greater tendency to engage in disordered eating behaviours." (3) mediation: "the impact of negative body image evaluation in disordered eating seems to be partially carried by higher body image-related cognitive fusion and lower body appreciation."
